message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights you typically enjoy as a renter: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights (Texas) | Notes | |----------|------------------------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for residential units; two months for furnished units.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | Landlords must itemize any deductions and provide receipts if requested. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain premises in a safe, sanitary condition.
• Must repair major structural issues, plumbing, heating, electrical, etc. | If landlord fails to fix, tenants may withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate the lease. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (except emergencies).
• Notice required: 24 hours for non-emergency entries. | Exceptions: emergencies, repairs, inspections with reasonable notice. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease must include: name of parties, address, rent amount, due date, security deposit, lease term, pet policy, etc.
• Landlord must provide written notice of any changes. | Oral leases are enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on rent increases, but must comply with local ordinances (e.g., Houston’s rent‑control rules).
• For month‑to‑month agreements, landlord must give at least 30 days’ notice before raising rent. | Some cities have rent‑increase caps. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, etc.
• Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in housing. | Applies to advertising, leasing, terms, and conditions. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve proper notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease termination).
• Eviction requires court action; unlawful detainer suit. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to repair, tenant may repair and deduct cost from rent (must follow procedure). | Must notify landlord in writing, keep receipts, and provide notice of intent to repair. | | **Pet Policy** | • Landlord may require a pet deposit or fee; cannot discriminate against pets unless they pose a health/safety risk. | Must be disclosed in lease. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Landlord may prohibit subletting, but must do so in writing.
• If prohibited, landlord cannot unreasonably deny a sublet. | Subletting may be allowed with landlord’s consent. | | **Notice of Termination** | • For month‑to‑month, either party must give 30 days’ written notice.
• For fixed-term, notice depends on lease length. | Notice must be in writing and delivered properly. | ### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Ensure it includes all required disclosures (security deposit limits, pet policy, maintenance responsibilities). 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of notices, emails, text messages, and photos of any damage or maintenance requests. 3. **Know Local Ordinances** – Some cities (Houston, Dallas, Austin) have additional tenant protections or rent‑control ordinances. 4. **Communicate in Writing** – When requesting repairs or notifying of problems, use written communication (email or certified mail) to create a record. 5. **Seek Legal Advice if Needed** – If your landlord violates your rights, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group. --- #### Quick Reference: How to File a Complaint | Issue | Where to File | Contact | |-------|---------------|---------| | Discrimination | U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) | https://www.hud.gov/complaint | | Unlawful Eviction | Texas Attorney General’s Office | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov | | Rent Dispute | Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs | https://www.tdhca.state.tx.us | If you’re facing a specific issue (e.g., landlord refusing to return a security deposit), let me know the details and I can help draft a formal letter or outline next steps.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. There's no request for generating a contract. So we don't need to call the function. Just answer.
